newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks surge after Fed leaves rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks surge after Fed leaves rates unchanged.

text.p: U.S. stocks leaped on Tuesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged at a closely watched meeting of its policy-making committee.

After the Fed's early afternoon announcement, the Dow Jones industrial average, which spent most of the session in negative territorry, immediately erased the deficit and stormed higher. The 30-stock average gained more than one percent to close unofficially up 75 at 7303.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index surged more than one percent to finish up 8.39 at 841.66 unofficially, within a whisker of its all-time record close of 841.88 on May 15.
Technology stocks were strong throughout the session, paced by Intel Corp's robust gains.

For the broader market, news of the Fed's decision brought some immediate relief. Beforehand, Wall Street analysts were sharply divided over whether the central bank would raise interest rates, with a slim majority polled by Reuters ahead of Tuesday's meeting expecting policy-makers to stand pat.
"It's good for the market short-term ... but it leaves some uncertainty about what the Fed is going to do long-term," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics.

That leaves a "cloud over the market," he said. "We can't really tell what (the Fed) thinks, which means the markets will ... be back to watching data piece by piece" for clues to whether the Fed will take action at its next policy meeting on July 1-2.
Other analysts agreed the Fed's decision to leave rates unchanged set the stage from some nervousness ahead.

"The market still confronts a dilemma. Only a steady deceleration in the U.S. economy would prevent the Fed from a July tightening and that means earnings disappointments," said Doug Cliggott, U.S. equity strategist at J.P. Morgan.
"On the other hand, if the economy picks up over the summer, the Fed comes back into play because we might need a tightening," he added.
At its March meeting, the central bank tightened its credit policy for the first time in more than two years, bumping up the federal funds target rate by a quarter percentage point.
The Dow industrials were boosted by sharp gains in International Business Machines Corp, transports and banking stocks.

IBM surged amid broad strength in technology stocks and a weaker dollar, which fell to a five-month low against the yen. Shares of other U.S.-based multinationals, including Procter & Gamble Co, also rose as the drop in the U.S. currency made their overseas sales more valuable.
Semiconductor stocks rode a wave of optimism after Merrill Lynch said it expected Intel's annual revenue growth to rise to 36 percent from 30 percent, traders said.
Intel surged 6-1/4 to 161. Applied Materials Inc added 3-13/16 to 69-15/16, and Altera Corp jumped 3-1/8 to 51-1/2.

Airline stocks surged in the wake of the Fed's announcement. UAL Corp, parent of United Airlines, rose 3-1/8 to 79-7/8. AMR Corp, parent of American Airlines, added 1-5/8 to 97-5/8, and Delta Air Lines gained 2-3/8 to 94-3/8.
Airlines are sensitive to rising interest rates because they usually carry high-debt loads.
The Dow transportation index gained 38.53 to 2673.64, an all-time high.
